newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X resumes trading, plunges C$12.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X resumes trading, plunges C$12.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd resumed trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange at 1500 EST/2000 GMT on Thursday, opening down C$12 at C$3.50.
The fall accelerated soon after, with the stock hitting C$2.65. Volume spiked within minutes to four million shares.
Minorca Resources Inc shares dropped C$3.35 to C$1.25 in turnover of nearly a million shares.
The fall shaved about C$3 billion from Bre-X's market capitalization.
Ten minutes after re-opening, the stock was down C$13.05, 84 percent below its Tuesday close of C$15.50. At the same time, Minorca was down C$3.34, or 73 percent, at C$1.30.
On Nasdaq, Bre-X was down US$9-1/2 at US$1-7/8.
Minorca and Bre-X have been halted since before the open on Wednesday. The TSE asked Bre-X for further information this morning and Bre-X issued a statement at 1358 EST/1858 GMT.

"Since Bre-X has provided the market with the current information known to the company concerning the confirmatory drilling conducted to date by Freeport-McMoRan (Copper & Gold Inc FCX.TO ) and the immediate plans of both Freeport and Bre-X for further work on the property, it is appropriate to re-open trading," the TSE said in a statement.
Bre-X also expressed its concerns to the Toronto Stock Exchange regarding the resumption of trading in Bre-X shares before an independent audit of its Busang findings is complete.
But the TSE said its task is to provide a continuous market in securities for investors.

"We understand that a gray market has developed in the U.S. to which only a limited group of investors has access, and the market is best served by a visible and accessible exchange," the exchange said.
It said waiting for the completion of the audit means it could take weeks or longer for definitive information to emerge.
"The exchange does not believe that it is appropriate to deprive shareholders and investors of a market for such a lengthy period of time," the TSE said.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
